problem:
The rate at which the cultivated area of a particular region grows $A(t),$ after $t$ years, can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=0.08A.
$$

How many years does it take for the cultivated area to increase by $40%?$ Round your answer to the nearest decimal place.
worked_solution:
We model the growth of the cultivated area using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}A}{\text{d}t}=0.08A.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
A(t)={A}_{0}\,{e}^{0.08t},
$$

where ${A}_{0}$ is the initial cultivated area.

Let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the cultivated area has increased by $40%.$ That is,

$$
A({t}_{1})=1.4{A}_{0}.
$$

We solve the above equation for ${t}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A({t}_{1}) & ={A}_{0}{e}^{0.08\cdot {t}_{1}} \\ 1.4{A}_{0} & ={A}_{0}{e}^{0.08{t}_{1}} \\ 1.4 & ={e}^{0.08{t}_{1}} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(1.4) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{0.08{t}_{1}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(1.4) & =0.08{t}_{1} \\ {t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(1.4)}{0.08} \\ {t}_{1} & ≈4.205\,9\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding to the nearest decimal place, we conclude that it takes $4.2$ years for the cultivated area to increase by $40%.$
